newsitem.title: HONG KONG: China says HK body to pass laws pre-handover - media.
newsitem.headline: China says HK body to pass laws pre-handover - media.

text.p: The provisional legislature, set to become Hong Kong's lawmaking body after Britain returns the territory to China, will pass laws before the handover, Beijing's top official on Hong Kong was quoted as saying.

Lu Ping, Director of China's Hong Kong and Macau Affairs Office, told a Hong Kong business delegation in Beijing on Thursday the provisional body had to start work now in advance of the change in sovereignty at midnight on June 30, local media reported on Friday.
China has vowed that the provisional chamber will replace the existing elected legislature, which came into existence after electoral reforms that angered Beijing.

"The provisional legislature can start its work, including passing some laws through their first, second and third readings so that there won't be a legal vacuum at the time of the handover," the South China Morning Post quoted Lu as saying.
"But the whole legislative procedure will only be completed and the laws become effective on July 1 when the chief executive will issue a decree to promulgate the laws.
"Strictly speaking, what the provisional legislature will do before July 1, 1997, is essential preparation. Its powers and functions will only begin to realise from the date of July 1."
China has promised in the past not to have two parallel legislatures operating in the territory before the handover.
The Democratic Party, Hong Kong's biggest pro-democracy group, has said it would challenge the legality of the provisional legislature if it passed laws before the handover.
The threat was repeated on Thursday when the party met with Chief Executive-designate Tung Chee-hwa.
Tung and the provisional legislature were chosen by the same body, the 400-member Selection Committee, whose members were picked by a Beijing-controlled council.
